title: Missouri congressional-map TRO expiry — the 14-day clock on Judge Clark's order compelling the 2025 map
source: NEWS: Chief U.S. District Judge Stephen R. Clark (E.D. Mo.) granted a temporary restraining order on 2026-09-08 barring Missouri's Secretary of State from 'implementing, using, publishing, distributing, or mandating the use of any congressional map other than the [2025 HB 1 plan] for the Nov. 3 election', reported as remaining in effect for 14 days pending a hearing on a preliminary injunction — Roll Call 2026-09-08 (fetched direct 2026-09-09), Democracy Docket 2026-09-08 (fetched direct 2026-09-09), NOTUS 2026-09-08 (fetched direct 2026-09-09, '...for two weeks while he considers whether to extend the use of the new map through November'). THE DATE IS COMPUTED, NOT READ OFF A SCHEDULING ORDER: Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(b)(2) expires a TRO 14 days after entry unless extended for good cause or by consent, and 2026-09-08 + 14 days = 2026-09-22. No fetched source named a preliminary-injunction hearing date, and the docket itself was not read this session. Filed estimate on three counts: the date is derived rather than published, this calendar has no confirmed source prefix for a court order, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. fox2now.com returned 403 on direct fetch and is not relied on
notes: Proposed by the missouri-map-ballot-deadline-2026-09-08 close-out (2026-09-09) as the next dated point in a fight that did NOT end on 09-08. Sequence that day: Justice Kavanaugh denied emergency application 26A304 (Hoskins v. von Glahn) without explanation and without dissents, leaving the Missouri Supreme Court's 09-03 judgment barring the 2025 map in force; minutes later Judge Clark granted this TRO in a separate suit by Republican congressional candidates (Rep. Bob Onder et al.), finding a 'high probability of success' on an Article I, Section 2 theory that the completed August 4 primary's ballots would otherwise be nullified, alongside an Equal Protection claim and a 'Purcell in reverse' argument. Two live orders now point opposite ways. People Not Politicians noticed an emergency appeal to the Eighth Circuit the same evening — that appeal carries NO date and is deliberately not proposed as an event; its absence here is a decision, not an oversight, and an Eighth Circuit ruling could moot this date entirely before it arrives. Not a market event: symbols: [], and the close-out measured the tape across the day two federal courts contradicted each other over a House seat — VIX 14.53 (09-04) to 15.72 (09-08), S&P 7718.60 to 7673.52 (-0.58%), with 09-08's named drivers being the 3-year note auction and pre-CPI positioning. Tracked as a seat-math input to midterm-elections-2026-11-03, and as a companion to missouri-uocava-ballot-mailing-2026-09-19, whose own research already established that the 09-19 UOCAVA date is not self-executing (52 U.S.C. 20302(g) waivers; enforcement by AG suit under 20307). If a scheduling order or docket entry later names the actual hearing or expiry date, this entry should be re-dated to it rather than defended.
